data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
#FLUX: -n 2
#FLUX: --setopt=mem-per-task=32G
#FLUX: -t 3d12h
#FLUX: --output={id}_<job-name>.out
#FLUX: --error={id}_<job-name>.err
#FLUX: --queue=<partition-name>

# The following SLURM directive was omitted as it has no direct Flux equivalent:
# #SBATCH --job-name=<job-name>
# Omission of job name may affect job tracking and log file naming conventions.

# The following SLURM directive was omitted as it has no direct Flux equivalent:
# #SBATCH --mail-user=<your-email>
# Flux does not have built-in support for email notifications via batch directives.

source /path/to/baseenv/bin/activate upstream

# select and edit the config file accordingly
snakemake --configfile=config/analysis.yaml all --cores 1 --unlock
snakemake --configfile=config/analysis.yaml all --cores 1 --rerun-incomplete

reasons: The directive '#FLUX: --setopt=mem-per-task=32G' is invalid. The '--setopt' flag is used for setting key-value store options, not for resource requests like memory.
issues: The job requests 2 tasks via '#FLUX: -n 2' but the snakemake commands are serial and configured to use only a single core ('--cores 1'). This will leave one of the two allocated tasks completely idle, wasting resources. The number of tasks should be reduced to 1, or the script should be modified to run tasks in parallel (e.g., using 'flux exec').

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --partition=<partition-name>
#SBATCH --job-name=<job-name>
#SBATCH --ntasks=2
#SBATCH --mem=64G
#SBATCH --mail-user=<your-email>
#SBATCH --time=03-12:00:00

#SBATCH --error=%j_%x.err

source /path/to/baseenv/bin/activate upstream

# select and edit the config file accordingly
